lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3 you met verbs and tenses. What is the past tense of "jump"? Jumped.
The -ing tenses show an action that goes on for a while.
Past: I was walking. Present: I am walking. Future: I will be walking. Use was or were, am, is or are, or will be, with the -ing word.
Helping verbs change the meaning: can means able to (I can swim). may means allowed to, or maybe (You may go. It may rain). must means have to (We must be kind).
Match the helper: we were building (not we was building); she is reading (not she are reading).
Try it in the world: while you build, say what you are doing ("I am building a bridge"). Say what you were doing ("I was digging"), and what you will be doing next. Next: adjectives and prepositions.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is happening now?
exercises.explain: "I am reading" is happening now.

exercises.prompt: Choose the helper: They ___ playing yesterday.
exercises.explain: Yesterday is past, and "they" takes "were".

exercises.prompt: Which word means "able to"?
exercises.hint: Think of "I ___ swim": which word says you are able to?
exercises.explain: "Can" means able to.

exercises.prompt: "I will be flying" tells about the future.
exercises.hint: Look for "will". Is it about now, the past or later?
exercises.explain: Yes: will be + -ing is the future.

exercises.prompt: Choose the helper: Right now, she ___ singing.
exercises.explain: Right now is the present, and "she" takes "is".

exercises.prompt: Choose the right verb: Tomorrow at noon we ___ sailing.
exercises.explain: Tomorrow is the future: we will be sailing.

exercises.prompt: Which word means you have to do it?
exercises.explain: "Must" means have to.

exercises.prompt: Which is correct?
exercises.explain: "We were building" is correct.

exercises.prompt: "You may leave the table" means you are allowed to leave.
exercises.explain: Yes: here "may" means allowed to.

exercises.prompt: Change to the past: "The dog is digging."
exercises.hint: In the past, "is" becomes which word?
exercises.explain: In the past, "is digging" becomes "was digging".

exercises.prompt: Which is correct?
exercises.explain: More than one: are dancing.

exercises.prompt: "Take an umbrella; it ___ rain later." Which word means maybe?
exercises.explain: "May" here means maybe.

exercises.prompt: Which tells about an action going on in the past?
choices: The owls were hooting all night.
exercises.explain: "Were hooting" is an action going on in the past.

exercises.prompt: "I can ride a bike" means I am allowed to ride a bike.
exercises.explain: No: can means able to. "I may ride a bike" would mean allowed to.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order.
exercises.explain: Next week I will be camping: the future -ing tense.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences by when the action goes on.
exercises.hint: Look at the helper: was/were, am/is/are, or will be.
exercises.explain: Was reading and were building are past. Is singing and am running are present. Will be sailing and will be flying are future.

exercises.prompt: Match each helping verb to its meaning.
exercises.hint: Try each in a sentence: I ___ swim; you ___ go; we ___ be kind.
exercises.explain: Can means able to; may means allowed to, or maybe; must means have to.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences by what the helping verb means.
exercises.hint: Swap in 'able to', 'allowed to', 'maybe' or 'have to': which one fits?
exercises.explain: Can means able to: I can swim, birds can fly. May means allowed to or maybe: you may go, it may rain. Must means have to: we must be kind, you must wear a helmet.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence to the helper that fits its gap.
exercises.hint: Look at the time words first, then check who is doing it.
exercises.explain: Yesterday is past: we were eating. Right now is present: the dog is digging. Tomorrow is future: I will be flying.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: the right helper, or the wrong one?
exercises.hint: Match the helper to the person: I am, he is, we were, you were.
exercises.explain: Right: we were, I am, he is. Wrong: it should be she is reading, they were singing and you were laughing.
